A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we present an autoencoder model with a novel latent space design that can be used to enforce disentanglement in an unsupervised manner and can be extended to utilize prior information.
we present a new type of autoencoder that allows for a principaled and flexible approach to disentanglement.
we present a model that combines the best properties of VAEs (e.g. disentanglement) and GANs (e.g, image quality and diversity), without the need for adversarial training.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a simple architectural modification to an autoencoder model can enable the use of prior information in a principled way, and can also enable disentanglement in latent spaces.
the latent space of a deep generative model can be used to modulate the output of the model, in a way that is independent from the input, while retaining high quality and diverse output samples.

a simple modification to a standard autoencoder can lead to an effective generative model that can be trained in an unsupervised fashion and that has the ability to modulate each layer of the decoder with a single vector.
